q: Which statement matches the Cambridge marking principle about errors?
o: Marks are not deducted for errors or omissions
Marks are deducted for every error
Half marks may be given for small errors
Marks depend on the student's grade target
why: Principle 3: marks are awarded positively and are not taken away for errors or omissions.

q: Can an examiner give a half mark?
o: No, marks are always whole marks
why: Principle 2: marks are always whole marks.

q: In a mark scheme, text in brackets ( ) means the text:
o: may be included but is not essential
is worth a mark by itself
why: The mark scheme says bracketed text may be included but is not essential.

q: When marking with a level descriptor, work convincingly meets the level. Which mark do you give?
o: The highest mark in the level
The lowest mark in the level
why: Convincingly meets the level means the top mark. Adequately means a middle mark. Just meets means the lowest mark.

q: Why should examiners not think about grade thresholds while marking?
o: Marks are based only on the mark scheme requirements
why: Principle 6: marks are based solely on the requirements in the mark scheme.

q: In June 2024 Exercise 1, which answer earns the mark for 'When was the term cosplay invented?'
why: The text says the activity started in 1939 but the name was created in 1984.

q: What type of cosplay does Lana prefer?
why: She likes science fiction but says fantasy is what she would choose first.

q: Question 6 asks for three details and has three marks. A student writes five correct details. How many marks?
why: The key says up to a maximum of three marks.

q: Which of these is a POLICY introduced to reduce car use in the June 2024 article?
why: Car-free zones is a policy. The other three are things the writer tried himself.

q: Which answer is acceptable for Question 9, what the writer tried to reduce his own car use?
o: charging drivers to enter the city
why: Sharing a car is something the writer did himself. The others are policies.

q: How many marks are there in Exercise 3 (Questions 8 and 9)?
why: Question 8 is 4 marks and Question 9 is 3 marks, so 7 in total.

q: In the June 2024 wild swimming task, who is the best match for 'explains why they avoid saying where they swim' (7b)?
why: Emine says regular swimmers value their private places.

q: Who is the best match for 'mentions being surprised to see wildlife while swimming' (7d)?
why: Ana describes a seal appearing next to her and says she did not expect it.

q: Who is the best match for 'will go wild swimming whatever the weather' (7f)?
why: Ana says it does not matter how cold or wet it is.

q: In ToddlerLab, why is Serena asked to wear special gloves (Question 12)?
o: So cameras can record her hand movements
To make her fingers easier to see
why: The gloves have reflective material so ceiling cameras can follow her hands.

q: What does 'as she does so' refer to in ToddlerLab Question 15?
why: It refers to running around the room, which is moving rapidly.

q: How are the 15 marks shared in Paper 1 Exercises 5 and 6?
o: Up to 6 for Content and up to 9 for Language
Up to 9 for Content and up to 6 for Language
why: Table A Content is up to 6 and Table B Language is up to 9.

q: What does the Content table assess?
o: Task fulfilment and development of ideas
why: Content covers task fulfilment (relevance, style, purpose and audience) and development of ideas.

q: How many questions are there in Paper 2 Listening and how many marks?
why: Paper 2 has 40 multiple-choice questions, each worth one mark.

q: In the June 2024 Listening key, what is the answer to Question 27?
why: Question 27 is in the multiple-matching exercise (Exercise 4) and the key gives G.
